subject: General Knowledge
description: HQ locations of UN bodies, financial, trade, defence organisations

questions.stem: The headquarters of the World Health Organisation (WHO) is in:
questions.explanation: WHO — established 1948, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. Six regional offices; India is in the SEARO office (New Delhi). Also HQed in Geneva — WTO, WIPO, ITU, UNHCR, ILO, WMO (all UN specialised agencies). UN itself is HQed in New York; UNESCO in Paris; WB and IMF in Washington DC; IAEA in Vienna.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is in:
questions.explanation: IMF and World Bank — both HQed in Washington DC, both set up by the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference, both starting in 1945. IMF — surveillance, lending to balance-of-payments crises (SDRs). World Bank — project finance for development. WTO — Geneva (successor to GATT since 1995). UN — New York (five main organs here; ICJ in The Hague).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the organisation with its headquarters. A. UNESCO. B. IAEA. C. WTO. D. OPEC. List-II: 1. Paris, 2. Vienna, 3. Geneva, 4. Vienna.
questions.explanation: UNESCO — Paris; IAEA — Vienna; WTO — Geneva; OPEC — Vienna. Other Vienna-based bodies — UNIDO, UNODC. Worth knowing — FAO and IFAD in Rome, UNICEF in New York, NATO in Brussels, Commonwealth Secretariat in London, ASEAN in Jakarta.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the UN's principal judicial organ, is located at:
questions.explanation: ICJ — based at the Peace Palace in The Hague (Netherlands) — is the only UN principal organ not in New York. Fifteen judges, elected by the UN General Assembly and the Security Council for 9-year terms. India's Dr Nagendra Singh served as ICJ President (1985-88); Justice Dalveer Bhandari is a current ICJ judge. The ICJ settles disputes between states; the ICC (also in The Hague) is a separate treaty court that tries individuals.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) succeeded which earlier treaty-based body in 1995?
questions.explanation: GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, 1947) ran through eight negotiation rounds; the last — the Uruguay Round (1986-94) — produced the Marrakesh Agreement establishing the WTO from 1 January 1995. WTO deals with trade in goods, services (GATS), intellectual property (TRIPS) and dispute settlement. India is a founding member. Headquarters — Geneva.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) has its Secretariat at:
questions.explanation: SAARC — founded in Dhaka in 1985 — has its Secretariat in Kathmandu, Nepal (operational since 1987). Eight members — India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Maldives (founding 7) + Afghanistan (2007). No full summit has been held since Kathmandu 2014 due to India-Pakistan tensions. ASEAN — Jakarta; BRICS Development Bank (NDB) — Shanghai.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) is in:
questions.explanation: FAO — established 1945, HQed in Rome. Companion Rome-based UN food bodies — WFP (World Food Programme, Nobel Peace 2020) and IFAD (International Fund for Agricultural Development). UNESCO — Paris; UN itself — New York; WHO / WTO — Geneva; IAEA / OPEC — Vienna.
